author: CJFAN
quote: genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience. After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience. The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favors either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging **** yes, I understand that 30 FPS is the intended experience, and I can tolerate 30 FPS when it's properly optimized. But the constant frame drops make an already sluggish experience considerably worse. There's a difference between accepting a locked 30 FPS and having to deal with unstable performance that makes the game borderline unplayable. Visual ambition means absolutely nothing when the actual gameplay feels this unpleasant.Ultimately, GTA VI is one of my biggest gaming disappointments. The hype, the budget, the development time, and the expectations meant absolutely nothing when the final experience failed to entertain me. I don't care how detailed the world is or how impressive the graphics might look. A beautiful open world cannot compensate for a terrible story, excessive sexual content, frustrating gameplay, and inconsistent performance. I wanted a great GTA game, not an overpriced exercise in patience. **I regret the time I spent playing it.**
